title: The session list refuses everyone it should, the same way

expect.why: No credential at all is unauthenticated, not forbidden. 403 would tell a caller their token was read and rejected, which is a different thing to debug.
The refusal body is the whole contract for a client that renders errors. Pinned exactly so no port invents its own wording or its own envelope.
A token that does not verify is indistinguishable from no token — saying which would tell an attacker whether a token was well-formed.
Byte-identical to the anonymous refusal, deliberately: a different message here is an oracle.
What every port's client library concludes from a 401. A library that reported success on a refusal would hand a caller an error body as data.
Observed under the library, which drops the status itself. Without this the matrix could not tell a 401 from a 403 or a 500.
The library agrees with the status it was given.
The list is a bare array, not an object wrapping one. A port that wrapped it would break every client's iteration.
An empty list is a legitimate answer; this asserts the shape can be counted at all.
